question: Around 29 % of EU citizens aged between 15 and 64 have tried illegal drugs at least once in their lifetime. Drug use causes numerous medical conditions and carries a high risk of dependency. Sadly, more and more young people are falling victim to drug use without receiving the necessary support by way of prevention and resolution of drug dependency problems.

What steps is the Commission actively taking together with Member States and what resources are being made available to prevent and combat drug use among young people and children in the context of the sharp rise in the number of young users in many EU Member States?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2024) The EU Drugs Strategy 2021-20251 and its Action Plan2 identify the priorities for the EU drug policy including addressing health-related aspects of drug use. In the area of drug demand reduction, the Strategy aims to contribute to the healthy and safe development of children and young people and to a reduction of the use of illicit drugs.

Increasing the availability of evidence-based targeted prevention interventions for young people is a priority area3. The Commission is evaluating the implementation of the Strategy and its Action Plan. The EU4Health’s Programme4 can support actions to complement measures of Member States in reducing damage to health due to illicit drug use.

In June 2023, the EU co-legislators adopted a legislation revising the mandate of the European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drug Addiction (EMCDDA). As of the 2nd of July 2024, the new EU Drugs Agency will have reinforced health and security threat assessment capabilities on drug-related threats and will promote evidence-based interventions to raise awareness on the adverse effects of drugs5.

At EU level, Council Framework Decision 2004/757/JHA6 lays down minimum rules and penalties to combat drug trafficking, which also apply to online activities, and allows to include new psychoactive substances within the definition of drugs on the basis of risk assessments carried out with EMCDDA.

Moreover, in order to address the increasing availability of drugs, including new psychoactive substances, to young people on social media platforms, the Commission developed within the EU Internet Forum7 a Knowledge Package on Combating Drug Sales Online, which aims to support social media companies in better moderating drugs content on their platforms.
